C. Basic plot using the Pokemon data

# Scatterplot of Attack vs. Speed for all Pokemon
# This lets us see whether faster Pokemon tend to hit harder
plot(
  x = pokemon_df$speed,
  y = pokemon_df$attack,
  main = "Pokemon Attack vs. Speed",
  xlab = "Speed",
  ylab = "Attack",
  col  = "steelblue",
  pch  = 16,       # solid circle points
  cex  = 0.7       # slightly smaller points to reduce overplotting
)

D. Summary table of the Pokemon data

# Use knitr::kable() to display a clean table of the first 10 rows
# Showing a subset of the most informative columns
library(knitr)

# Select a readable subset of columns for the preview table
pokemon_preview <- pokemon_df[1:10, c("pokemon", "type_1", "hp", "attack",
                                    "defense", "speed", "generation_id")]

# Render the table with a caption
kable(pokemon_preview,
      caption = "First 10 Pokemon: Selected Statistics",
      align   = "lcccccr")

F. Extracting a numeric vector and applying a simple calculation

# Extract the 'hp' column as a standalone numeric vector
hp_values <- pokemon_df$hp

# Calculate the mean HP across all Pokemon
mean_hp <- mean(hp_values, na.rm = TRUE)

# Print the result with a clear label
cat("Mean HP across all Pokemon:", round(mean_hp, 2), "\n")
## Mean HP across all Pokemon: 68.95

G. Applying two vectorized mathematical operations to a numeric vector

# Use the 'attack' column for both operations
attack_values <- pokemon_df$attack

# Operation 1: Scale attack to a 0-100 index
# Subtract the minimum, then divide by the range — vectorized across all values
attack_scaled <- (attack_values - min(attack_values, na.rm = TRUE)) /
                 (max(attack_values, na.rm = TRUE) - min(attack_values, na.rm = TRUE)) * 100

# Operation 2: Apply a log transformation to compress the scale
# Adding 1 avoids log(0) for any Pokemon with 0 attack
attack_log <- log(attack_values + 1)

# Preview the first 6 values of each transformed vector side by side
head(data.frame(
  original    = attack_values,
  scaled_0_100 = round(attack_scaled, 2),
  log_transformed = round(attack_log, 3)
))
##   original scaled_0_100 log_transformed
## 1       49        23.78           3.912
## 2       62        30.81           4.143
## 3       82        41.62           4.419
## 4       52        25.41           3.970
## 5       64        31.89           4.174
## 6       84        42.70           4.443
